exact_target: There exists a finite universal C such that for every n >= 1, every full-dimensional log-concave probability measure mu on R^n with mean zero and Cov(mu)=I, and every locally Lipschitz f in L2(mu), Var_mu(f) <= C integral |gradient f|^2 dmu. Equivalently after an affine change, C_P(mu) <= C ||Cov(mu)||_op; the lower bound ||Cov(mu)||_op <= C_P(mu) follows from linear functions. Cheeger constants use the boundary/min(mass,1-mass) convention and equivalence up to universal constants, not equality of constants.
